narrative.text: Margrave Lucan Vael receives you in the same drawing room where he first offered you a slot in the Thornfeld Opportunity Trust. The room has not changed. The fund, however, has performed. He places a distribution statement on the table between you. Your 5,000 VK investment is now worth 15,000 VK — a return of three hundred percent in under a year. The statement lists the other twelve investors who received identical distributions. Their names are a roster of Veltrian power: two former finance ministers, the chairman of the banking association, three industrialists, a retired general, and the widow of President Halvek. You are now on the same list they are.

The fund has had an excellent year, Chancellor. Your presence in the portfolio has been noted — favorably — by the other limited partners. They are people who value discretion, but they are also people who notice who is in the room and who is not. You are in the room. That has made certain conversations easier. Certain investments more attractive. Certain obstacles smaller than they might otherwise have been. The distribution is 15,000 VK. You may take it as cash, or you may reinvest it. I would recommend reinvestment — next year's returns are projected to be even stronger. Of course, there is also the question of whether certain investigative bodies — the BCA, for instance, or certain journalists — might take an interest in the fund's membership. I have taken precautions. I assume you have as well.

Fifteen thousand VK. Three times what I put in. More money than most Veltrian families earn in a decade. And it comes with Vael's implicit reminder: I am now one of them — listed alongside Halvek's widow and the financial architecture of twenty-six years of authoritarian rule. If the BCA is funded and investigating, this distribution is evidence. If Nadia Voss is looking into oligarchs, my name is on a document she would very much like to find. I could take the money and stay entangled. I could reinvest and deepen the relationship. Or I could divest — return the capital, refuse the distribution, attempt to sever the connection before it becomes evidence in someone else's investigation. Vael is watching to see which I choose. He will not be the only one.

choices.text: "I will take the distribution in cash, Lucan. Fifteen thousand VK. The investment was legal, the fund is private, and I am entitled to the return on my capital the same as any other partner. I did not direct government policy to benefit the fund. I did not share confidential information with its managers. If someone wants to argue that membership in an investment fund constitutes corruption, let them make that argument — and let them explain why twelve other prominent Veltrians are also in the fund and somehow not under investigation. I invested. I profited. That is how investment works. The fact that I am Chancellor does not strip me of the right to participate in the economy."

"Reinvest the distribution. All fifteen thousand — back into the Thornfeld Trust, compounded for the next cycle. I am not here for a one-time return, Lucan. I am here because the people in this room are the people who determine whether this country functions. If I am going to govern effectively, I need to be in the room. The return is attractive, but the access is more valuable. Reinvest. And let the other partners know that the Chancellor is not a short-term investor — she is a long-term partner. That should make certain conversations even easier."

"Liquidate my position, Lucan. Return my original 5,000 VK. Donate the 10,000 VK profit — not to my account, but to an independent anti-corruption foundation of the administrator's choosing. And remove my name from the list of limited partners. I am grateful for the return. I am not grateful for the entanglement. Every decision I make that benefits any of the other twelve partners — and there have been decisions, whether I intended them or not — now looks like a quid pro quo. I cannot govern effectively if I am perceived as beholden to this room. I cannot be the Chancellor the country needs if I am on the same investor list as the widow of the man whose legacy I was elected to dismantle. The investment is closed. The relationship is not — but it is now at arm's length, which is where it should have been from the beginning."
